translation:
But the moving vessel on the dorsum of the foot is connected above to the Chong (衝) vessel and the Shaoyin and Yangming (陽明) channels; one should only needle it shallowly, and must not let blood without stopping. [Figure: Diagram of the points to be needled 11]
The Lingshu, Treatise on Cold and Heat Diseases (寒熱病篇), says: When the body is injured and much blood comes out, and one is struck by wind and cold, or if one has fallen from a height and the four limbs are slack and do not gather, it is called body lassitude (體惰); take the three crossings (三結交) below the navel in the lower abdomen. The three crossings are Yangming and Taiyin (太陰); three cun below the navel is Guanyuan (關元).
